title: Exploring the human-animal bond, with Maggie O’Haire, PhD

sentences.en: In August, Congress passed the PAWS Act, puppies assisting wounded service members, directing
sentences.zh: 今年八月，国会通过了《PAWS法案》，即“为受伤军人提供协助的幼犬法案”，要求

sentences.en: the Department of Veterans Affairs to begin a pilot program to fund service dogs for veterans with post-traumatic stress disorder.
sentences.zh: 退伍军人事务部启动一项试点计划，为患有创伤后应激障碍的退伍军人资助服务犬。

sentences.en: It's a reflection of an emerging field of research that is finding that trained service dogs can help people cope with post-traumatic stress disorder.
sentences.zh: 这反映了一个正在兴起的科研领域，该领域发现经过训练的服务犬可以帮助人们应对创伤后应激障碍。

sentences.en: The VA is not the only place interested in the power of animals to help heal and comfort humans.
sentences.zh: 退伍军人事务部并不是唯一一个关注动物帮助人类疗愈和慰藉之力量的机构。

sentences.en: In recent years, therapy dogs have shown up in hospitals, on college campuses at exam time, and even in offices where management is looking for ways to reduce workers' stress.
sentences.zh: 近年来，治疗犬出现在医院、考试期间的大学校园，甚至出现在管理层寻找方法来减轻员工压力的办公室里。

sentences.en: At the same time, though, emotional support animals have become a favorite butt of late-night
sentences.zh: 然而与此同时，情感支持动物也成为了深夜

sentences.en: TV jokes conjuring images of people boarding planes with peacocks and hamsters in tow.
sentences.zh: 电视节目的调侃对象，让人联想起人们带着孔雀和仓鼠登机的画面。

sentences.en: So what does the research say about the effectiveness of animal-assisted therapy?
sentences.zh: 那么，研究对于动物辅助治疗的效果是怎么说的呢？

sentences.en: When can animals help reduce distress and improve our mental health?
sentences.zh: 动物在什么时候能够帮助减轻痛苦并改善我们的心理健康？

sentences.en: What's the difference among service animals, therapy animals, and emotional support animals?
sentences.zh: 服务动物、治疗动物和情感支持动物之间有什么区别？

sentences.en: What's backed by research and what is not?
sentences.zh: 哪些是有研究支持的，哪些是没有的？

sentences.en: And what about regular household pets?
sentences.zh: 还有普通的家养宠物呢？

sentences.en: How do our companion animals affect our health and well-being?
sentences.zh: 我们的伴侣动物如何影响我们的健康和幸福？

sentences.en: Do our pets make us healthier and happier?
sentences.zh: 宠物是否让我们更健康、更快乐？

sentences.en: Welcome to Speaking of Psychology, the flagship podcast of the American Psychological Association that examines the links between psychological science and everyday life.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《心理学说话》，这是美国心理学会的旗舰播客节目，主要探讨心理科学与日常生活之间的联系。

sentences.en: I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 我是金·米尔斯。

sentences.en: Our guest today is Dr. Maggie O'Hare.
sentences.zh: 我们今天的嘉宾是玛吉·奥黑尔博士。

sentences.en: Dr. O'Hare is a psychologist and an associate professor of animal-human interaction at the Purdue
sentences.zh: 奥黑尔博士是一名心理学家，也是普渡

sentences.en: University College of Veterinary Medicine.
sentences.zh: 大学兽医学院的人与动物互动副教授。

sentences.en: Her research focuses on the ways that humans interact with animals, including both household pets and highly-trained service animals.
sentences.zh: 她的研究重点是人类与动物互动的方式，包括家养宠物和高度训练的服务犬。

sentences.en: She runs National Institute of Health-funded studies on the effects of service dogs on veterans
sentences.zh: 她主持了由美国国立卫生研究院资助的研究，探讨服务犬对患有

sentences.en: with post-traumatic stress disorder and on animal-assisted interventions for children with autism.
sentences.zh: 创伤后应激障碍的退伍军人的影响，以及对自闭症儿童的动物辅助干预。

sentences.en: She has published dozens of peer-reviewed publications and textbook chapters, and her work has been covered widely in the media, including The Wall Street Journal,
sentences.zh: 她发表了数十篇同行评审出版物和教科书章节，她的工作在媒体上得到了广泛报道，包括《华尔街日报》、

sentences.en: The New York Times, and National Public Radio.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》和全国公共广播电台。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你。

sentences.en: Thank you for joining us today, Dr. O'Hare.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你今天加入我们，奥黑尔博士。

sentences.en: Thank you so much for having me.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢邀请我来。

sentences.en: It's my pleasure.
sentences.zh: 这是我的荣幸。

sentences.en: Let's start by defining what we're talking about when we discuss the different types of animals that I mentioned in the introduction, service animals, emotional support animals,
sentences.zh: 让我们首先来定义一下，当我们讨论我在引言中提到不同类型的动物时，我们到底在谈论什么，服务动物、情感支持动物、

sentences.en: therapy dogs.
sentences.zh: 治疗犬。

sentences.en: These terms get thrown around, and I think mixed up by people who think they're interchangeable, but they're not.
sentences.zh: 这些术语经常被提及，我认为人们会把它们混淆，以为它们是可以互换的，但事实并非如此。

sentences.en: So can you tell us a little bit about what these terms mean and the differences among them?
sentences.zh: 你能给我们简单介绍一下这些术语的含义以及它们之间的区别吗？

sentences.en: Absolutely, because I do agree.
sentences.zh: 当然可以，因为我完全同意。

sentences.en: People get confused about this, and it's important at the start to figure out what we're talking about.
sentences.zh: 人们对此感到困惑，所以在开始时弄清楚我们在谈论什么非常重要。

sentences.en: And kind of if we take a step back, what we see is that the roles for dogs in our society are increasing, and that's why we have these different niches of where dogs are helping.
sentences.zh: 而且如果我们退一步来看，我们看到的是狗狗在我们社会中的角色正在增加，这就是为什么我们在狗狗提供帮助的地方看到了这些不同的细分领域。

sentences.en: So the first category is a therapy dog.
sentences.zh: 所以第一类是治疗犬。

sentences.en: These are intended to provide comfort to individuals in different medical, residential, or academic settings.
sentences.zh: 这些旨在为不同的医疗、居住或学术环境中的个人提供慰藉。

sentences.en: So if you think about, as an example, nursing homes where a dog might come in and visit, or hospitals where a dog might come and visit a child who is receiving treatments.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你想想，举个例子，狗狗可能会进来探访的疗养院，或者狗狗可能会探访接受治疗的儿童的医院。

sentences.en: These are someone's personal dogs that they volunteer as a therapy dog to bring in and provide comfort to many different individuals.
sentences.zh: 这些是某个人的私家犬，他们作为志愿者将它们作为治疗犬带进来，为许多不同的人提供慰藉。

sentences.en: The second category is an emotional support dog.
sentences.zh: 第二类是情感支持犬。

sentences.en: These are medically prescribed for one specific individual to provide therapeutic benefits through dedicated companionship.
sentences.zh: 这些是通过专门的陪伴为某一个特定个人医疗处方以提供治疗效益的犬只。

sentences.en: So instead of visiting many people in many settings, the emotional support dog stays with that one person.
sentences.zh: 所以情感支持犬不会去很多环境中探访许多人，而是留在那个特定的人身边。

sentences.en: And then the final category, potentially, of the highest level of rigor and training is the service dog.
sentences.zh: 然后最后一类，可能具有最高级别的严格性和训练要求，那就是服务犬。

sentences.en: And that is a dog that is trained to do a specific task to help mitigate a disability.
sentences.zh: 这是一种经过训练去执行特定任务以帮助减轻残疾的狗狗。

sentences.en: And that's really what distinguishes that service dog from emotional support dog.
sentences.zh: 这确实是将服务犬与情感支持犬区分开来的地方。

sentences.en: The emotional support dog doesn't need to be trained to do a specific task and doesn't need to be with someone with a specific disability.
sentences.zh: 情感支持犬不需要接受训练来执行特定任务，也不需要与有特定残疾的人在一起。

sentences.en: Now, you're mentioning dogs specifically, but I think there are other animals that can be involved in some aspects of this type of work, right?
sentences.zh: 现在，你专门提到了狗，但我认为还有其他动物也可以参与这种工作的某些方面，对吧？

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: So if you're looking at a service animal, there are two species that can be service animals.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你看服务动物，有两类物种可以成为服务动物。

sentences.en: Are you aware of what those two are?
sentences.zh: 你知道那是哪两种吗？

sentences.en: Do you know what the backup outside of a dog is?
sentences.zh: 你知道除了狗之外的备选是什么吗？

sentences.en: I don't.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Well, that's exciting that we can learn today.
sentences.zh: 嗯，今天能学到新知识真是令人兴奋。

sentences.en: So the other species that can be a service animal is a miniature horse, actually.
sentences.zh: 所以可以成为服务动物的另一个物种，实际上是小型马。

sentences.en: So that, you know, the logic behind that, there's a similar lifespan, a similar trainability, similar size in some cases.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，这背后的逻辑是，它们有相似的寿命、相似的可训性、在某些情况下相似的体型。

sentences.en: And so although it is vastly less common, it is legally permissible to have a miniature horse as a service animal.
sentences.zh: 因此，尽管它远没有那么常见，但在法律上允许将小型马作为服务动物。

sentences.en: Now, if you talk about emotional support animals, there are no species restrictions.
sentences.zh: 现在，如果你谈论情感支持动物，则没有任何物种限制。

sentences.en: So that does mean that technically anyone can have any species as their emotional support animal.
sentences.zh: 所以这确实意味着从技术上讲，任何人都可以将任何物种作为他们的情感支持动物。

sentences.en: Where there are some nuances are really airlines.
sentences.zh: 存在一些细微差别的地方实际上是航空公司。

sentences.en: So airlines used to say, if you have an emotional support animal, they can come on the plane.
sentences.zh: 所以航空公司过去常常说，如果你有情感支持动物，它们就可以上飞机。

sentences.en: Then they battened down the hatches a little bit and said only if they're specific species.
sentences.zh: 然后他们稍微收紧了政策，说只有特定物种才可以。

sentences.en: And now many airlines have moved further to only service animals that are allowed to travel with people on airlines.
sentences.zh: 现在许多航空公司进一步采取措施，只允许服务犬与人一起在航空公司旅行。

sentences.en: So where you are able to have that emotional support animal is really in your home of any species that you'd like.
sentences.zh: 所以你能够拥有情感支持动物的地方实际上是在你的家里，可以是任何你想要的物种。

sentences.en: One of your main research projects is looking at the effects of service dogs on the mental health and wellness of military members diagnosed with PTSD and also their families.
sentences.zh: 你的主要研究项目之一是调查服务犬对被诊断患有创伤后应激障碍的军人及其家人的心理健康和福祉的影响。

sentences.en: What have you found?
sentences.zh: 你们发现了什么？

sentences.en: How can service dogs help people with PTSD?
sentences.zh: 服务犬如何帮助患有创伤后应激障碍的人？

sentences.en: What exactly does the dog do?
sentences.zh: 狗具体做什么？

sentences.en: We've been studying military veterans with PTSD in their families for the past six or seven years now.
sentences.zh: 在过去的六七年里，我们一直在研究患有创伤后应激障碍的退伍军人及其家属。

sentences.en: And so what we've been able to do thus far is really compare cohorts of individuals who have a service dog to those who don't have a service dog.
sentences.zh: 因此，到目前为止，我们能够做到的是真正比较拥有服务犬的个人群体与没有服务犬的个人群体。

sentences.en: And what we find repeatedly in each study is that veterans with service dogs show clinically lower levels of PTSD symptomology than those who do not have a service dog.
sentences.zh: 我们在每项研究中反复发现的是，拥有服务犬的退伍军人表现出的创伤后应激障碍症状水平在临床上低于没有服务犬的人。

sentences.en: Now, obviously, it's limited to those individuals who are interested in a service dog who wanted that in the first place.
sentences.zh: 现在，很显然，这仅限于那些对服务犬感兴趣、一开始就想要服务犬的个人。

sentences.en: But we do see that their symptoms are presenting at lower levels.
sentences.zh: 但我们确实看到他们的症状表现处于较低水平。

sentences.en: We see that they have less absenteeism from work and an overall greater quality of life through their self-report.
sentences.zh: 根据他们的自我报告，我们看到他们因病缺勤的情况减少，总体生活质量更高。

sentences.en: And when we dig deeper into that, what we find is that they have trained tasks that they're using, right?
sentences.zh: 当我们深入探究这一点时，我们发现他们有在使用的经过训练的任务，对吧？

sentences.en: Because as a service animal, it's there to help the disability.
sentences.zh: 因为作为服务动物，它的存在是为了帮助应对残疾。

sentences.en: And by and large, the most common task they're using is to help address their anxiety symptoMs.
sentences.zh: 总的来说，他们最常使用的任务是帮助应对焦虑症状。

sentences.en: So on average, about three to five times a day, they'll use some sort of task or command to have the dog help them with their anxiety.
sentences.zh: 因此，平均而言，他们每天大约使用三到五次某种任务或指令，让狗帮助他们应对焦虑。

sentences.en: So that might be asking the dog to lean up against them for deep pressure.
sentences.zh: 所以这可能包括要求狗靠在他们身上以提供深层压力。

sentences.en: That might be the dog noticing the individual is about to have a panic attack and nudging them
sentences.zh: 这可能是狗注意到这个人即将发作恐慌症并推他们一下，

sentences.en: to trigger them to come back to the present, take deep breaths and be mindful as a couple of examples of how the dogs are helping.
sentences.zh: 以促使他们回到当下、深呼吸并保持正念，这是狗如何提供帮助的几个例子。

sentences.en: So what we're trying to do is bring data behind these anecdotes that we hear.
sentences.zh: 所以我们正在努力为我们听到的这些轶事提供数据支持。

sentences.en: You know, so many veterans have said to us, I would not be alive if it were not for my service dog.
sentences.zh: 你知道，很多退伍军人对我们说，如果没有我的服务犬，我早就活不成了。

sentences.en: And although, you know, that is emotionally salient for me and meaningful for many, what, you know, doctors, policymakers, insurance companies are looking for is the data behind
sentences.zh: 虽然，你知道，这对我来说具有情感上的显著意义，对许多人来说意义重大，但你知道的，医生、决策者、保险公司寻找的是背后的

sentences.en: that.
sentences.zh: 数据。

sentences.en: And that's what we're hoping to pull together and what we've been able to do so far.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们希望汇集的内容，也是我们迄今为止能够做到的事情。

sentences.en: One interesting point that you've made is that there are some potential drawbacks, including the fact that service dogs make visible what is essentially an invisible disability.
sentences.zh: 你提出的一个有趣观点是，存在一些潜在的弊端，包括服务犬将本质上看不见的残疾变得显而易见这一事实。

sentences.en: Can you talk about that?
sentences.zh: 你能谈谈这个吗？

sentences.en: Is that a concern for many of the veterans that you've worked with?
sentences.zh: 这会是你合作过的许多退伍军人所关心的问题吗？

sentences.en: You know, when we look at any form of animal assisted intervention or service animal, any treatment, really, intervention, we want to ask, what is it doing well and what's an
sentences.zh: 你知道，当我们看待任何形式的动物辅助干预或服务动物时，实际上是任何治疗或干预，我们都想问，它做得好的地方是什么，可以改进的

sentences.en: area where it can improve?
sentences.zh: 领域是什么？

sentences.en: And we were interested to find that for veterans, the biggest drawback or challenge, I suppose,
sentences.zh: 我们很有兴趣发现，对退伍军人来说，他们提出的最大的弊端或挑战，我想，

sentences.en: that they do bring up is that, yes, when they're walking around in society without the dog, nobody notices them in the same way.
sentences.zh: 是，是的，当他们在社会中没有狗陪伴四处走动时，没有人会以同样的方式注意到他们。

sentences.en: But when they have their dog, people tend to love dogs and want to say hello and want to learn more.
sentences.zh: 但当他们带着狗时，人们往往喜欢狗，想要打招呼并想了解更多。

sentences.en: And so it draws attention to them.
sentences.zh: 因此，这把注意力吸引到了他们身上。

sentences.en: And for some veterans, they say, you know what?
sentences.zh: 对于一些退伍军人来说，他们说，你知道吗？

sentences.en: It's been good for me.
sentences.zh: 这对我有好处。

sentences.en: It brings me out of my shell.
sentences.zh: 它让我走出了封闭的内心。

sentences.en: I talk to people more.
sentences.zh: 我跟人说话更多了。

sentences.en: They show interest in me.
sentences.zh: 他们对表现出兴趣。

sentences.en: And for other veterans, they say, I just want to go to the store and buy some milk.
sentences.zh: 而对于其他退伍军人，他们说，我只是想去商店买点牛奶。

sentences.en: I don't want to be the subject of attention or interaction.
sentences.zh: 我不想成为关注或互动的主角。

sentences.en: And I think that draws attention to the fact that we might need some more public education
sentences.zh: 我认为这引起了人们的注意，即我们可能需要围绕这一点开展更多公众教育，

sentences.en: around this, around how to behave around people's service animals and how to be respectful.
sentences.zh: 教导人们如何在他人的服务动物周围表现以及如何保持尊重。

sentences.en: You've also studied animal assisted interventions for kids with autism, including with service dogs, but also in some of your earlier work with guinea pigs in classrooMs.
sentences.zh: 你还研究了针对自闭症儿童的动物辅助干预，包括使用服务犬，以及在你早期的一些研究中在教室里使用豚鼠。

sentences.en: First of all, how did you end up with guinea pigs of all animals?
sentences.zh: 首先，在所有动物中，你最终怎么会养起豚鼠的？

sentences.en: And then what did you find in that research?
sentences.zh: 然后你在那项研究中发现了什么？

sentences.en: How do these animals help kids with autism?
sentences.zh: 这些动物是如何帮助自闭症儿童的？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Well, thank you for asking about that.
sentences.zh: 嗯，谢谢你问起这个。

sentences.en: I think it's a fun story now.
sentences.zh: 我觉得现在这是一个有趣的故事。

sentences.en: At the time, it was actually, it came out of a few challenges that arose.
sentences.zh: 当时，其实它源于出现的一些挑战。

sentences.en: So, you know, I did my bachelor's degree in psychology, and then I applied to do a Fulbright fellowship in Australia to study service dogs for autism.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，我攻读了心理学学士学位，然后我申请去澳大利亚获得富布赖特奖学金，研究用于自闭症的服务犬。

sentences.en: It was the perfect pairing.
sentences.zh: 这是完美的搭配。

sentences.en: It was going to be with a veterinarian and a psychologist, and the whole project would be so exciting.
sentences.zh: 它将由兽医和心理学家共同参与，整个项目将非常令人兴奋。

sentences.en: So I flew.
sentences.zh: 所以我飞了过去。

sentences.en: I graduated with my degree in hand.
sentences.zh: 我手拿着学位毕业了。

sentences.en: I flew to Australia.
sentences.zh: 我飞往澳大利亚。

sentences.en: I arrived, slightly jet lagged, and I went straight to the university to meet with my mentorship team for this project.
sentences.zh: 我到达时，带着轻微的时差，我直接去了大学，与这个项目的导师团队会面。

sentences.en: And I was informed, well, the psychologist has quit, and we don't have any funding for the project.
sentences.zh: 我被告知，心理学家已经辞职了，我们没有这个项目的任何资金。

sentences.en: And so, welcome.
sentences.zh: 所以，欢迎来到这里。

sentences.en: Go home?
sentences.zh: 回家吗？

sentences.en: Well, that's exactly, Kim, what I questioned myself in that moment.
sentences.zh: 嗯，金，我在那一刻确实这样质问过自己。

sentences.en: You know, I finished the meeting, and I had this long walk home.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我结束了会议，走了很长一段路回家。

sentences.en: It was a long walk because I wasn't exactly sure where I was going in foreign territory.
sentences.zh: 这是一段漫长的路，因为我并不完全确定我在陌生的领地上要去哪里。

sentences.en: A good time to think.
sentences.zh: 这是思考的好时机。

sentences.en: And, you know, I reflected, and I thought, do I turn around?
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，我反思了，我想，我要转身吗？

sentences.en: Do I go home?
sentences.zh: 我要回家吗？

sentences.en: Is this a message that this isn't going to happen?
sentences.zh: 这是一个暗示这不会发生的信号吗？

sentences.en: And on that walk, I really thought to myself, no, I want to study this.
sentences.zh: 在那段路上，我真的对自己说，不，我想研究这个。

sentences.en: So what I did is, first, I learned to apply for a grant.
sentences.zh: 所以我做的第一件事是学会申请资助。

sentences.en: I didn't know what that word meant before, but I did that.
sentences.zh: 我以前不知道这个词是什么意思，但我做了。

sentences.en: And second, I had to find another source of animal.
sentences.zh: 第二，我必须找到另一种动物来源。

sentences.en: You know, service dogs are expensive.
sentences.zh: 你知道，服务犬很昂贵。

sentences.en: I had no funding.
sentences.zh: 我没有资金。

sentences.en: So what I found out was that the local vet school was doing research on guinea pigs.
sentences.zh: 所以我发现当地的兽医学校正在对豚鼠进行研究。

sentences.en: And the type of research they did is they were breeding the animals, and then after day two of the guinea pig's life, they didn't need them.
sentences.zh: 他们做的研究类型是繁殖这些动物，然后在豚鼠出生后的第二天，他们就不需要它们了。

sentences.en: So they would either euthanize the animal or give them to me for free.
sentences.zh: 所以他们要么对动物实施安乐死，要么免费把它们送给我。

sentences.en: And so that was a very convenient and cost-effective model.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个非常方便且具有成本效益的模型。

sentences.en: I socialized the guinea pigs from that young age and developed a classroom-based intervention program.
sentences.zh: 我从那么小的年纪开始就对豚鼠进行社会化训练，并开发了一个基于教室的干预项目。

sentences.en: And what I actually learned is that the guinea pigs were quite a scalable intervention, you know?
sentences.zh: 我真正学到的是，豚鼠是一种非常具有可扩展性的干预措施，你知道吗？

sentences.en: Not every classroom has the capacity to afford and care for a dog in it.
sentences.zh: 并不是每个教室都有能力负担并照顾一只狗。

sentences.en: But with the guinea pigs, we could have a housing enclosure in the classroom that was consistent and stable.
sentences.zh: 但有了豚鼠，我们可以在教室里建立一个始终如一且稳定的饲养围栏。

sentences.en: And what we found is that for many of the kids, having that there at all times, when they felt stressed, they could go sit next to the cage and watch the animals.
sentences.zh: 我们发现的是，对许多孩子来说，随时都有这个东西在，当他们感到压力时，他们可以坐在笼子旁边看动物。

sentences.en: And what we also found was that although for many adults, a dog seems more exciting than a guinea pig, for these children, they were so excited about these little creatures that
sentences.zh: 我们还发现，尽管对许多成年人来说，狗似乎比豚鼠更令人兴奋，但对这些孩子来说，他们对这些小生物感到非常兴奋，

sentences.en: they were going to learn to care for and nurture.
sentences.zh: 他们将学会照顾和抚育它们。

sentences.en: And honestly, it turned out to be a blessing in disguise.
sentences.zh: 老实说，这结果证明是因祸得福。

sentences.en: Well, how did the children improve?
sentences.zh: 嗯，孩子们是如何改善的？

sentences.en: I mean, were they more socialized than to deal with other children?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们比以前更善于社交来与其他人相处吗？

sentences.en: Or was it just because they, you know, related to the animals?
sentences.zh: 还是仅仅因为他们，你知道，与动物产生了共鸣？

sentences.en: We found many different things from this program.
sentences.zh: 我们在这次项目中发现了许多不同的情况。

sentences.en: So we were looking at children with autism spectrum disorder in mainstream or inclusion classrooMs.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们当时正在研究主流或融合课堂中的自闭症谱系障碍儿童。

sentences.en: So we studied not only the child with autism, but also some of their typically developing peers.
sentences.zh: 所以我们不仅研究了患有自闭症的儿童，还研究了他们的一些正常发育同龄人。

sentences.en: And what we found is that the children with autism were able to integrate more with their peers when the animal was present.
sentences.zh: 我们发现，当有动物在场时，自闭症儿童能够更好地融入同龄人中。

sentences.en: They were talking more with their peers.
sentences.zh: 他们与同龄人交流得更多了。

sentences.en: They were looking at their peers more.
sentences.zh: 他们注视同龄人的时间变多了。

sentences.en: They were smiling, laughing, and engaging more.
sentences.zh: 他们的微笑、大笑和互动也增多了。

sentences.en: And we used a comparison condition of toys.
sentences.zh: 而且我们还设置了一个以玩具作为对照的条件。

sentences.en: So we compared the guinea pigs to toys.
sentences.zh: 所以我们将豚鼠与玩具进行了对比。

sentences.en: And as you know, you know, toys are designed, built, and sold to elicit engagement from children.
sentences.zh: 如你所知，玩具的设计、制造和销售本来就是为了激发孩子们的互动。

sentences.en: And so the fact that a guinea pig who's not doing anything particularly special could elicit more social behaviors was fascinating to us as we commenced in this field.
sentences.zh: 因此，一只其实并没有做什么特别事情的豚鼠，竟然能激发出更多的社交行为，这让我们这些刚进入这个领域的人感到非常神奇。

sentences.en: And that was in the moment behavioral changes.
sentences.zh: 这只是当时的即时行为变化。

sentences.en: But we also saw, you know, broader changes over time.
sentences.zh: 但我们也看到了，随着时间的推移，出现了一些更广泛的变化。

sentences.en: Teachers and parents were reporting more social engagement, more social skills, and less challenging behaviors in the classroom as well.
sentences.zh: 老师和家长也报告说，课堂上的社会交往增多了，社交技能提高了，具有挑战性的行为减少了。

sentences.en: Let's switch gears for a minute and talk about household pets.
sentences.zh: 我们换个话题，聊聊家养宠物。

sentences.en: It's probably obvious to a lot of people that pets make us happy.
sentences.zh: 对很多人来说，宠物能让我们快乐，这或许是显而易见的。

sentences.en: But is there research that supports the idea that pets are good for our physical and mental health?
sentences.zh: 但有没有研究来支持“宠物对我们的身心健康有益”这一观点呢？

sentences.en: What does the data say?
sentences.zh: 数据是怎么说的？

sentences.en: What does the data say?
sentences.zh: 数据到底是怎么说的？

sentences.en: That is what I eat, sleep, and breathe in my role.
sentences.zh: 这就是我日常工作中全身心投入的事情。

sentences.en: So I'm glad that you asked.
sentences.zh: 所以我很高兴你问了这个问题。

sentences.en: And it's interesting because I think that many people or potentially pet owners or pet lovers will say, it's obvious.
sentences.zh: 这很有趣，因为我认为许多人、潜在的宠物主人或宠物爱好者会说，这是显而易见的。

sentences.en: We already know this.
sentences.zh: 我们早就知道了。

sentences.en: Why would we study it?
sentences.zh: 为什么还要去研究它？

sentences.en: But in actuality, you know, in some of the top psychology journals, people have questioned
sentences.zh: 但实际上，在一些顶尖的心理学期刊上，有人对此提出了质疑

sentences.en: that and said, is this a mere hypothesis rather than, you know, a supported fact empirically?
sentences.zh: 并指出，这究竟仅仅是一个假设，还是一个经过实证支持的事实？

sentences.en: And I think one of the challenges comes from the way we study it, right?
sentences.zh: 我认为挑战之一来自于我们研究它的方式，对吧？

sentences.en: It's a lot of it is correlational in nature, meaning that we don't know if the animal caused
sentences.zh: 很大程度上它本质上是相关性的，这意味着我们不知道究竟是动物带来了

sentences.en: improved mental health or people with higher mental health to begin with go out to adopt or purchase an animal.
sentences.zh: 更好的心理健康，还是本来心理健康水平就较高的人更倾向于去领养或购买动物。

sentences.en: So we're trying to tease that apart through different studies.
sentences.zh: 所以我们正试图通过不同的研究来厘清这一点。

sentences.en: And some of the best ways we can do that is look at when you're with the animal versus not.
sentences.zh: 我们可以采用的最佳方法之一，就是观察你和动物在一起与不在一起时的区别。

sentences.en: And we do find that when you're with the animal, you smile and talk to people more.
sentences.zh: 我们确实发现，当你和动物在一起时，你笑得更多，也更愿意和人说话。

sentences.en: You show changes in your physiology, whether that be increases in oxytocin or what's called
sentences.zh: 你的生理指标会发生变化，无论是催产素（也就是所谓的

sentences.en: the love hormone or reductions in your anxious arousal, such as heart rate or blood pressure.
sentences.zh: “爱的荷尔蒙”）水平的上升，还是心率或血压等焦虑唤醒状态的降低。

sentences.en: We are able to see these momentary changes.
sentences.zh: 我们能够观察到这些短暂的即时变化。

sentences.en: And I think where the field is moving is to find out whether these are related to long-term lasting or broader gains.
sentences.zh: 我认为该领域目前的发展方向，是去探究这些变化是否与长期、持久或更广泛的收益相关。

sentences.en: And it's just been challenging because it's harder to randomize someone to get a dog versus not get a dog.
sentences.zh: 这一直很有挑战性，因为很难随机安排一个人去养狗或不养狗。

sentences.en: You know, humans are autonomous and when they want to get a dog, they're going to go ahead and get it regardless of whether you want to assign that to them in the study.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，人类是自主的，当他们想养狗时，无论你是否在研究中这样分配，他们都会去养。

sentences.en: So I think we also gain a lot of knowledge from our service and therapy animal studies, although it is different.
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得我们也从服务动物和治疗动物的研究中获取了大量知识，尽管它们有所不同。

sentences.en: Those are groups where we can randomize and we can have that built-in waiting period to try and extrapolate some of the changes we see there to pet ownership.
sentences.zh: 在这些群体中，我们可以进行随机分组，并设置固定的等待期，从而尝试将我们在那里观察到的一些变化推演到宠物饲养上。

sentences.en: I think we need to take that with some caveats, though, because a service animal is often bred
sentences.zh: 不过我认为，我们在接受这些结论时需要带有一些保留意见，因为服务动物通常经过专门的

sentences.en: and trained and prepared specifically to be wonderful for the human and to behave, you know, in specific ways, whereas our companion animals aren't always behaving or performing
sentences.zh: 繁育、训练和准备，以便完美地配合人类并以特定方式行事，而我们的伴侣动物并不总是能表现或展示出

sentences.en: at that level.
sentences.zh: 那种水平。

sentences.en: So I think that one of the key things that I like to talk with new or potential companion animal owners about is managing those expectations.
sentences.zh: 因此，我认为与新晋或潜在的伴侣动物主人沟通时，关键的事情之一就是管理好这些期望。

sentences.en: You know, I think there's this dichotomy that we see.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我认为我们看到了这样一种二分法。

sentences.en: You know, some people say this pets are good for everything and they're amazing.
sentences.zh: 有些人说宠物百利而无一害，它们太棒了。

sentences.en: And some people talk just about the challenges.
sentences.zh: 而有些人则只谈论其中的种种挑战。

sentences.en: And I think ultimately it's a balance.
sentences.zh: 我认为归根结底这需要平衡。

sentences.en: And I think if owners can go in knowing, hey, the initial phases, there'll be some growing pains.
sentences.zh: 我想如果主人在开始时就有所心理准备——嘿，初期会有一些成长的烦恼。

sentences.en: You'll have to learn about each other.
sentences.zh: 你们需要互相了解。

sentences.en: If you have a puppy or a small animal, there's going to be potty training.
sentences.zh: 如果你养的是一只小狗或小动物，就会面临如厕训练。

sentences.en: But if you can build that bond and move through those initial tough phases, that's when you'll
sentences.zh: 但如果你能建立那种羁绊并度过最初艰难的阶段，你就会

sentences.en: start to see some of those broader, longer term gains when you develop that rich and intimate bond with the other creature.
sentences.zh: 开始看到更广泛、更长远的收益，当你与这个小生命建立起丰富而亲密的羁绊时。

sentences.en: Are there differences among the kinds of animals that we have as pets?
sentences.zh: 我们当作宠物的动物种类之间是否存在差异？

sentences.en: Is there something, you know, you always feel like, well, if you can hold the animal, if it's tactile, then that, you know, is going to, you'll feel that in a more gut, on a gut
sentences.zh: 是不是有一种感觉，如果你能抱住这只动物，如果它具有触感，那么你就会在更深层的直觉上

sentences.en: level, as opposed to having goldfish.
sentences.zh: 感受到这一点，而不是养金鱼。

sentences.en: Or even if you have a, you know, a tiny pet, like a mouse or a rat, where you can't, you know, you can't really hug it because you're going to hurt it.
sentences.zh: 甚至如果你养的是一只小宠物，比如老鼠，你不能，你知道的，你不能真正拥抱它，因为你会弄伤它。

sentences.en: Does that make a difference in the way that people react?
sentences.zh: 这会改变人们的反应方式吗？

sentences.en: Are they healthier or happier with certain kinds of animals as compared to others?
sentences.zh: 与饲养其他动物相比，饲养某些特定动物的人会更健康或更快乐吗？

sentences.en: I think there are absolutely species differences.
sentences.zh: 我认为物种之间绝对存在差异。

sentences.en: And I think you tapped into a really key element of that.
sentences.zh: 并且我认为你切中了其中一个非常关键的要素。

sentences.en: And that's that physical tactile element.
sentences.zh: 那就是身体触觉要素。

sentences.en: But I think it's not necessarily that one's better than the other, but it's different.
sentences.zh: 但我认为这不一定意味着一种比另一种更好，而是它们有所不同。

sentences.en: So if you think about potentially fish tanks, we've had some really interesting studies that show how your heart rate and your blood pressure are lowered when you're looking
sentences.zh: 因此，如果你想一想鱼缸，我们做过一些非常有趣的研究，表明当你看着鱼缸时，你的心率和血压会降低

sentences.en: at the fish tank.
sentences.zh: 看着鱼缸里的鱼。

sentences.en: And so following studies like that, I mean, you're hard pressed to find a doctor's office or waiting room that doesn't have a fish tank.
sentences.zh: 所以在这些研究之后，我的意思是，你很难找到一个没有鱼缸的医生办公室或候诊室。

sentences.en: Because after those studies came out, people realized that if it's going to reduce your anxious arousal, we want to have that in places that are going to become stressful to center
sentences.zh: 因为在这些研究发表后，人们意识到如果它能减少你的焦虑唤醒，我们就希望把它放在那些会让人感到压力的地方，来集中

sentences.en: your attention.
sentences.zh: 你的注意力。

sentences.en: So we have this theory, it's called the biophilia hypothesis, and it's been around for decades.
sentences.zh: 所以我们有一个理论，叫做生物亲和假说，它已经存在几十了。

sentences.en: And it's the idea that as humans, evolutionarily, we're primed to look at animals in nature.
sentences.zh: 这个观点是，作为人类，在进化过程中，我们天生就倾向于关注自然界的动物。

sentences.en: And we have this, you know, unconscious bias to attend to that.
sentences.zh: 我们有一种无意识的偏好去关注这些。

sentences.en: And when we have that external positive focus of attention, it can reduce our anxiety and our arousal.
sentences.zh: 当我们把外部注意力积极地聚焦于此，它就能减轻我们的焦虑和唤醒水平。

sentences.en: And so that's, you know, this species that we can't interact with physically, those things happen.
sentences.zh: 所以，即使是对于我们无法进行身体互动的物种，这些效果也会发生。

sentences.en: Even when it's an animal that we typically would like to pet or interact with physically, if we just watch a video of those animals, we will see similar outcomes.
sentences.zh: 即使是我们通常喜欢抚摸或进行身体互动的动物，如果我们只是观看它们的视频，也会看到类似的结果。

sentences.en: So I think you're gathering those benefits.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为你同样能从中获得这些益处。

sentences.en: And then when you do move into the place where you're able to physically interact with the animal, I think there's several different things that can happen.
sentences.zh: 然后，当你真正进入能够与动物进行物理互动的阶段时，我认为会发生几种不同的事情。

sentences.en: I think that that soft contact touch has been related to reductions in anxiety and arousal and also to increases in some of our bonding and social neuroscience love hormones
sentences.zh: 我认为那种柔和的接触已被证实与焦虑和唤醒的降低有关，同时也与我们体内一些社交神经科学中涉及结合和爱的荷尔蒙（如催产素）的增加有关

sentences.en: such as oxytocin.
sentences.zh: 比如催产素。

sentences.en: So we're triggering those other elements.
sentences.zh: 所以我们正在触发这些其他的成分。

sentences.en: And I think that over time, if we look at social relationships and bonding, probably the touch piece is important in developing that over time.
sentences.zh: 我认为随着时间的推移，如果我们审视社会关系和羁绊，触摸这一环节可能在随着时间推移培养这种关系方面起着重要作用。

sentences.en: Though you might talk to a reptile or fish owner that argues quite differently.
sentences.zh: 尽管你可能会从爬行动物或鱼类饲养员那里听到截然不同的争论。

sentences.en: You know, I have certainly met people who talk so fondly about the bond they've developed with other creatures.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我确实遇到过这样的人，他们深情地谈论自己与其他动物建立的羁绊。

sentences.en: But I would say on the whole, yes, that contact does play a key role in the bonding element.
sentences.zh: 但我可以说总体而言，是的，这种接触确实在建立羁绊的过程中发挥了关键作用。

sentences.en: I think somewhere in that answer, I heard you say something that explains why we love to watch cat videos.
sentences.zh: 我想在那个回答的某处，我听到你说了一些话，解释了为什么我们那么喜欢看猫咪视频。

sentences.en: You know, that is a big one there.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这确实是一个大热门。

sentences.en: Whenever I am lecturing about how we have this affinity to look at life and lifelike creatures, I do show elements of cat videos.
sentences.zh: 每当我讲授关于我们如何对生命和类生命生物抱有这种亲和力时，我都会展示猫咪视频的片段。

sentences.en: You know, there's something called the Internet Cat Video Festival that's been going on for many years now, which I myself have not attended.
sentences.zh: 你知道，有一个举办了很多年的活动叫做互联网猫咪视频节，我自己还没去参加过。

sentences.en: But it's from what I understand, people watching videos of cats together.
sentences.zh: 但据我所知，那是人们聚在一起观看猫咪视频的活动。

sentences.en: And there have been studies looking at, you know, when you watch cute animal videos, how that affects your level of attention and your mood.
sentences.zh: 并且有研究探讨了当你观看可爱动物视频时，它如何影响你的注意力和情绪水平。

sentences.en: And it does seem like when we have absence of the real thing, watching a video does a pretty good job.
sentences.zh: 看来，在我们无法接触到真正的动物时，观看视频确实能起到相当不错的效果。

sentences.en: So let's talk a little bit about emotional support animals.
sentences.zh: 那我们来聊聊情感支持动物吧。

sentences.en: We had years of these viral news stories about people bringing peacocks and kangaroos onto airplanes.
sentences.zh: 我们曾有多年关于人们把孔雀和袋鼠带上飞机的病毒式新闻报道。

sentences.en: And then in December, TSA announced that airlines would no longer be required to accommodate emotional support animals, only trained service animals, as you said earlier.
sentences.zh: 接着在12月，美国运输安全管理局宣布，航空公司将不再被要求为情感支持动物提供便利，正如你刚才所说，现在只认可经过训练的服务动物。

sentences.en: Is there research out there on whether these emotional support animals actually do help people cope with mental illness and emotional distress?
sentences.zh: 是否有研究表明这些情感支持动物确实能帮助人们应对精神疾病和情感困扰？

sentences.en: Is this really a valid therapeutic treatment?
sentences.zh: 这真的算是一种有效的治疗手段吗？

sentences.en: I think this is a growing area where we need more research.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一个不断发展的领域，我们需要更多的研究。

sentences.en: But what I will say is that if you think about a companion animal versus an emotional support animal, I mean, what companion animal isn't potentially providing emotional support?
sentences.zh: 但我想说的是，如果你把伴侣动物和情感支持动物进行比较，我的意思是，哪种伴侣动物没有潜在地提供情感支持呢？

sentences.en: So I do think that we can draw on the literature we have about companion animals for broader impacts.
sentences.zh: 所以我确实认为我们可以借鉴现有的关于伴侣动物对产生更广泛影响的文献。

sentences.en: And we can see that there are benefits that could be gained.
sentences.zh: 我们可以看到其中确实存在可以获得的益处。

sentences.en: But I don't think we have much research yet that's really digging into emotional support animals specifically.
sentences.zh: 但我认为我们目前还没有太多的研究真正深入探讨专门的情感支持动物。

sentences.en: We've really started with companion animals and service animals.
sentences.zh: 我们实际上是从伴侣动物和服务动物开始研究的。

sentences.en: And I think emotional support animals will be our next big area to look into.
sentences.zh: 我认为情感支持动物将是我们接下来要深入研究的一个大领域。

sentences.en: So let's talk about your career for a moment.
sentences.zh: 那么我们来谈谈你的职业生涯吧。

sentences.en: You have a very unusual situation where you work in a veterinary school as a psychologiSt.
sentences.zh: 你有一个非常不同寻常的职位，身为心理学家的你在兽医学院工作。

sentences.en: My understanding is that you are one of one or two people who are in this position right now.
sentences.zh: 据我所知，你目前是处于这个职位的仅有的少数几个人之一。

sentences.en: I mean, and how is it different for a psychologist working in a veterinary school as opposed to being just in a psychology department someplace?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，心理学家在兽医学院工作，与仅仅在某地的心理学系工作有什么不同？

sentences.en: It's a lot of fun.
sentences.zh: 这非常有趣。

sentences.en: So, you know, I've been in psychology departments and I've been in the College of Veterinary Medicine, and you are correct.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，我曾在心理学系待过，也曾在兽医学院待过，你的看法是正确的。

sentences.en: There's only, you know, one other tenure track psychologist in a College of Veterinary
sentences.zh: 据我所知，目前在兽医学院里担任终身轨心理学教授的

sentences.en: Medicine that I'm aware of at the moment.
sentences.zh: 据我所知，目前只有另外一位。

sentences.en: And I would say the main difference in working in the vet school versus psychology department is whether or not you have to defend what you do all day.
sentences.zh: 我想说的是，在兽医学院工作与在心理学系工作的主要区别在于，你是否需要为自己整天在做的事情进行辩护。

sentences.en: So I think that in, you know, traditional streams of psychology, this isn't something that comes up in Psych 101.
sentences.zh: 因此我认为，在传统的心理学流派中，这并不是心理学入门101里会涉及的内容。

sentences.en: It doesn't come up in your training.
sentences.zh: 它不会出现在你的培训中。

sentences.en: And so it is kind of a more niche field.
sentences.zh: 所以这算是一个更小众的领域。

sentences.en: And when I was in psychology, I had to defend why it was a rigorous field of study.
sentences.zh: 当我在心理学系时，我必须为这为什么是一个严谨的研究领域进行辩护。

sentences.en: In the vet school, no one asks me questions.
sentences.zh: 在兽医学院，没有人会质问我。

sentences.en: They accept and acknowledge and know how important it is because they see it every single day.
sentences.zh: 他们接受、认可并深知这一点有多重要，因为他们每天都能亲眼看到。

sentences.en: So I have to say, for me, it was so fun to be, you know, invited to do this podcast because my background, my training's in psychology.
sentences.zh: 所以我必须说，对我而言，受邀来做这个播客非常有趣，因为我的背景和培训都在心理学领域。

sentences.en: I think it's the field where we should be studying this.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是我们应该开展研究的领域。

sentences.en: And I don't think it has always been accepted as much as it has been in recent years.
sentences.zh: 我不认为它过去一直像近年来这样被广泛接受。

sentences.en: And I think a lot of that has to do with, you know, once the National Institutes of Health started funding this, people took it a bit more seriously.
sentences.zh: 我认为这很大程度上是因为，一旦美国国立卫生研究院开始资助这项研究，人们就更加严肃对待它了。

sentences.en: And now I also think that clinicians are seeing so many requests for a service animal, a therapy animal, animal-assisted intervention.
sentences.zh: 现在我也认为，临床医生看到了如此多关于服务动物、治疗动物以及动物辅助干预的需求。

sentences.en: And they are looking for data to answer those questions.
sentences.zh: 他们正在寻找数据来回答这些问题。

sentences.en: And so I'm so excited to be able to share that data and inform our field.
sentences.zh: 所以我非常兴奋能够分享这些数据并为我们的领域提供参考。

sentences.en: How did you get interested in studying human-animal interaction?
sentences.zh: 你是如何对研究人与动物互动产生兴趣的？

sentences.en: Was this something that you were always interested in?
sentences.zh: 这是你一直以来就很感兴趣的事情吗？

sentences.en: Or did you start in a more typical human-only psychology program?
sentences.zh: 还是说你最初也是从更传统的纯人类心理学项目开始的？

sentences.en: I absolutely started in the typical way, in a human-only psychology program.
sentences.zh: 我绝对是从最典型的方式开始的，也就是纯人类的心理学项目。

sentences.en: And it was actually during my undergrad degree.
sentences.zh: 实际上是在我读本科期间。

sentences.en: You know, in psych classes, they will let you choose your own topic.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，在心理学课上，他们会让你选择自己的课题。

sentences.en: And naively, I thought I was inventing my own topic when I decided to think about the impact of animals on children's empathy.
sentences.zh: 当时我很天真地以为，当我决定研究动物对儿童同理心的影响时，我是在创造自己的全新课题。

sentences.en: As I started to look into it, I found it's actually a field where people are studying it.
sentences.zh: 当我开始深入了解时，我发现这其实是一个已经有人在研究的领域。

sentences.en: And I went to college at Vassar College in New York.
sentences.zh: 我在纽约的瓦萨学院上的大学。

sentences.en: And there was a place just 45 minutes away called the Green Chimney School, which is a world leader in providing therapy animals in a school residential setting.
sentences.zh: 在仅仅45分钟车程远的地方，有一个叫做“绿色烟囱学校”的地方，它是学校寄宿环境中提供治疗动物的世界领导者。

sentences.en: So what I did is I reached out to Green Chimneys and I said, hey, what research are you doing?
sentences.zh: 所以我联系了绿色烟囱学校，我说，嘿，你们在做哪些研究？

sentences.en: Can I do an internship?
sentences.zh: 我可以来实习吗？

sentences.en: Can I help you out?
sentences.zh: 我能帮上什么忙吗？

sentences.en: And they said, hi, we do not accept interns that we don't have a program.
sentences.zh: 他们说，你好，我们不接受实习生，我们没有这个项目。

sentences.en: We're not doing that much research.
sentences.zh: 我们没有做那么多研究。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Goodbye.
sentences.zh: 再见。

sentences.en: And for better or for worse, based on my personality, I persisted and said, you know, I have some ideas.
sentences.zh: 不管好坏，基于我的性格，我坚持了下来，我说，你知道的，我有一些想法。

sentences.en: I think I could come in once a week and help you, you know, set up informed consent and conduct research and really track these outcomes.
sentences.zh: 我想我可以每周来一次，帮你们建立知情同意书、开展研究并真正追踪这些结果。

sentences.en: And their clinical department was amazing and took me on and let me start this journey with them.
sentences.zh: 他们的临床部门非常棒，接纳了我，并让我与他们一起开启了这段旅程。

sentences.en: And that one thing led to another.
sentences.zh: 就这样一环扣一环。

sentences.en: And I realized that I could keep pushing it.
sentences.zh: 我意识到我可以继续推进它。

sentences.en: What I will say is that all along the way, I was advised not to make this my career.
sentences.zh: 我要说的是，一路走来，我都曾被劝告不要把这作为我的职业。

sentences.en: So I was definitely advised to pick something mainstream.
sentences.zh: 我绝对被建议去选择更主流的方向。

sentences.en: You have to have, you know, you need it to be developmental.
sentences.zh: 你必须选择发展心理学。

sentences.en: You need it to be social.
sentences.zh: 你需要做社会心理学。

sentences.en: You need it to be something that's in our career lines that we're used to seeing.
sentences.zh: 你需要它符合我们职业生涯中常见的那种方向。

sentences.en: And I decided to ignore that advice and continue to pursue my passion.
sentences.zh: 而我决定忽视这个建议，继续追求我的热情。

sentences.en: And I feel very fortunate that it worked out and that I can now run my own lab and study this and spend my days, you know, digging into the psychology behind why we interact with
sentences.zh: 我感到非常幸运，结果一切顺利，我现在能够运营自己的实验室来研究这个课题，把每天的时间花在深入研究我们与动物互动背后的心理学上，

sentences.en: animals, how it impacts our mental health and wellness.
sentences.zh: 以及它如何影响我们的心理健康和福祉。

sentences.en: And I'm heartened to see that I think there are a growing number of careers in this area.
sentences.zh: 我很高兴地看到，这个领域的职业选择似乎正在不断增加。

sentences.en: I'm not sure that everyone should ignore the advice to have a mainstream path to fall back on.
sentences.zh: 我不确定每个人都应该忽视“留一条主流后路”的建议。

sentences.en: But I think that, you know, adding this into your portfolio is a growing trend.
sentences.zh: 但我认为，把这一点加入你的职业组合中是一种越来越明显的趋势。

sentences.en: Did Purdue create this slot and you applied for it?
sentences.zh: 是普渡大学设立了这个岗位，然后你申请的吗？

sentences.en: Or did you go to them and tell them that they need somebody like you in their veterinary school?
sentences.zh: 还是你主动联系他们，告诉他们兽医学院需要像你这样的人才？

sentences.en: How did that happen?
sentences.zh: 这到底是怎么回事？

sentences.en: So my first NIH grant that I got, I was in Australia and partnered with Purdue University because they were in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 我获得的第一笔美国国立卫生研究院（NIH）资助时，我正在澳大利亚，并与普渡大学合作，因为他们在美利坚合众国。

sentences.en: And it was easier to, you know, fund something from the U.S.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，从美国政府那里获得资助相对更容易一些，

sentences.en: government in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 这笔资金在美国发放。

sentences.en: And I formed a partnership with Purdue through that grant.
sentences.zh: 通过那笔资助，我与普渡大学建立了合作关系。

sentences.en: And when they opened up a new position, they called me and said, you know, we don't typically have a psychology PhD researcher fill this type of role, but we'd love for you to come
sentences.zh: 当他们开放一个新的职位时，他们打电话给我说，我们通常不会让心理学博士研究员来担任这类角色，但我们很乐意邀请你来

sentences.en: out and interview.
sentences.zh: 实地面试。

sentences.en: And, you know, they didn't hate what I had to say in my job talk.
sentences.zh: 而且，他们在我的学术报告中并没有对我所说的话感到反感。

sentences.en: So we were able to forge a partnership.
sentences.zh: 所以我们得以建立合作关系。

sentences.en: And Purdue has had the Center for Human-Animal Bonds since the late 1980s.
sentences.zh: 普渡大学自20世纪80年代末以来就设有“人与动物纽带中心”。

sentences.en: So they have had a center focused on this for quite some time.
sentences.zh: 所以他们设立专注于此的中心已经有相当长的一段时间了。

sentences.en: They just haven't built in that psychology piece.
sentences.zh: 只是他们还没有建立起心理学这块拼图。

sentences.en: So what are the big open questions?
sentences.zh: 那么，目前重大的未解问题有哪些呢？

sentences.en: What are you looking at?
sentences.zh: 你正在关注什么？

sentences.en: What do you hope to do going forward and well into the future?
sentences.zh: 你希望在未来乃至更长远的未来做些什么？

sentences.en: Well into the future.
sentences.zh: 在遥远的未来。

sentences.en: Well, I hope that this field continues to grow.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我希望这个领域能继续发展壮大。

sentences.en: It is so much fun and it feels so meaningful.
sentences.zh: 它太有趣了，而且意义重大。

sentences.en: I mean, when you have people telling you that an animal saved their life and they would
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，当你听到有人说动物拯救了他们的生命，如果不是因为心理健康问题，他们

sentences.en: not be alive due to their mental health challenges, the ability to work with them to create data
sentences.zh: 可能已经不在人世了，此时能够与他们合作，通过数据创造出

sentences.en: that shares their story through numbers, through science, it's just, it's so meaningful and it's so much fun.
sentences.zh: 用数字和科学来分享他们的故事，这种感觉真的太有意义、太有趣了。

sentences.en: And I hope that I get to do that for many years to come and I hope others do as well.
sentences.zh: 我希望在未来的许多年里都能继续做这件事，也希望其他人能够加入进来。

sentences.en: So that's my passion and my goal.
sentences.zh: 这就是我的热情所在和我的目标。

sentences.en: And in terms of the specific questions, you know, my immediate next step is to continue to work with the veterans and service dogs.
sentences.zh: 至于具体的问题，我接下来的直接步骤是继续与退伍军人和服务犬合作。

sentences.en: So we just received a five-year NIH grant to do a randomized clinical trial of the efficacy of service dogs for veterans and their families.
sentences.zh: 我们最近刚获得美国国立卫生研究院为期五年的资助，用于对退伍军人及其家属使用服务犬的疗效进行随机对照临床试验。

sentences.en: So that will certainly keep us busy for a few years here.
sentences.zh: 这肯定会让我们在未来几年里忙个不停。

sentences.en: I'm really hoping to get that rigorous data on a clinical level to share with clinicians, with doctors, with insurance companies, with policymakers.
sentences.zh: 我真的很希望能获得这种临床层面的严谨数据，以便与临床医生、医生、保险公司和政策制定者分享。

sentences.en: That's our initial next step.
sentences.zh: 这是我们最初的下一步。

sentences.en: And then kind of on a broader level, I have so many open questions, but, you know, to boil it down, I would say I'm excited about the physiology pieces.
sentences.zh: 从更广泛的层面来说，我还有很多未解的问题，但总的来说，我对生理学方面的内容感到非常兴奋。

sentences.en: I think it's fascinating that we can objectively track differences when someone's with an animal versus without.
sentences.zh: 我认为非常迷人的一点是，我们可以客观地追踪一个人在有动物陪伴与没有动物陪伴时的生理差异。

sentences.en: You know, if we take, for example, the service dogs, we found that veterans who had a service dog had a different cortisol profile than those who didn't.
sentences.zh: 举个例子，就拿服务犬来说，我们发现拥有服务犬的退伍军人具有与没有服务犬的人不同的皮质醇特征。

sentences.en: So if we look at stress hormone physiology and see that it is significantly different when you
sentences.zh: 因此，如果我们观察应激激素生理学，会发现当你

sentences.en: have a service dog, that fascinates me and that makes me ask questions about mechanisMs.
sentences.zh: 拥有服务犬时，它有显著的不同，这让我着迷，也让我开始探讨其作用机制。

sentences.en: How does it work?
sentences.zh: 它是如何起作用的？

sentences.en: Why does it work?
sentences.zh: 为什么它能起作用？

sentences.en: And can we pursue that further?
sentences.zh: 我们能对此进行更深入的探究吗？

sentences.en: So the physiology is one piece.
sentences.zh: 所以生理学是一个方面。

sentences.en: And then the second piece that I'd love to look into, which I would venture to say is less popular, is that, you know, I think there's this drive for people because they are so
sentences.zh: 我想深入探讨的第二个方面——我敢说这可能不太受欢迎——那就是，我认为人们因为对它充满热情，有一种倾向，想要非黑即白地看待问题，认为这对我们太好了。

sentences.en: passionate about it to have it be black and white, to say this is so good for us.
sentences.zh: 这对每个人都好。

sentences.en: It's great for everyone.
sentences.zh: 给每个人都安排上。

sentences.en: Sign everyone up.
sentences.zh: 而我希望能看到更多的细微差别，去弄清楚在什么人身上、在什么情况下这种做法效果最好，以及我们该如何将其改进得更好。

sentences.en: And what I'd love to see is more nuance to find out for who and under what circumstances this is best and how can we make it better.
sentences.zh: 我不认为你开发出一款药——如果我们以药物试验为例——开发完之后就说它已经完成了，然后就不管了。

sentences.en: I don't think that you develop, if we think about drug trials as an example, you don't develop a drug, move on and say it's done.
sentences.zh: 你会想要改进它。

sentences.en: You know, you want to enhance it.
sentences.zh: 你想要减少副作用。

sentences.en: You want to reduce side effects.
sentences.zh: 你想要简化流程。

sentences.en: You want to streamline it.
sentences.zh: 我也希望能在我们的动物辅助干预中做到这一点。

sentences.en: And I want to be able to do that with our animal-assisted interventions.
sentences.zh: 我们怎样才能让这种干预对人类和动物都达到最佳效果呢？

sentences.en: How can we make this the best for the human and for the animal?
sentences.zh: 我想如果我们能够更深入地挖掘，我们将能够进行更坦诚的对话，并为所有相关人员带来更好的流程。

sentences.en: And I think if we're able to, you know, dig deeper, we'll be able to have more honest conversations and make it a better process for everyone involved.
sentences.zh: 好吧，这次访谈真的非常有趣。

sentences.en: Well, this has been really interesting.
sentences.zh: 奥黑尔博士，和你交谈我很开心。

sentences.en: I've enjoyed talking to you, Dr. O'Hare.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你今天做客我们的节目。

sentences.en: Thank you for joining us today.
sentences.zh: 这是我的荣幸。

sentences.en: It was my pleasure.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢邀请我来参加。
